dimensions.assessment: Affects direct support professionals, home- and community-based service providers, and federal statistical agencies.
dimensions.evidence: establish a separate code for direct support professionals as a healthcare support occupation

dimensions.assessment: Modifies statistical occupational classification systems and data collection categories rather than directly altering benefits or wages.
dimensions.evidence: The Standard Occupational Classification system is designed and maintained solely for statistical purposes

dimensions.assessment: Explicitly authorizes no additional funds to be appropriated.
dimensions.evidence: No additional funds are authorized to be appropriated to carry out this Act.

dimensions.assessment: Directs the OMB to consider a specific occupational reclassification and submit a report if declined.
dimensions.evidence: The Director of the Office of Management and Budget shall... consider revising the Standard Occupational Classification system to establish a separate code

dimensions.assessment: Applies to the first SOC system revision occurring after enactment, with a one-time reporting requirement if the change is not made.
dimensions.evidence: as part of the first revision of the Standard Occupational Classification system occurring after the date of enactment

missing_information: Any potential long-term statistical or indirect economic impacts of establishing a new occupational code.
importance_detail.rationale: The bill directs the Office of Management and Budget to consider establishing a separate Standard Occupational Classification code for direct support professionals and report to Congress if it decides not to do so, explicitly authorizing no new funds.
